idea: Data centre and digital infrastructure property research
pain: Data centre economics blend construction, power and tech in ways generalists cannot assess
v1: A primer on UK/EU data centre development economics
verdict: Hottest real assets theme, needs exactly her cross-domain lens, and infra funds pay well.

why.distribution: Infrastructure funds are reachable through her network, though they are adjacent to her direct peer group.
why.demand: Infra funds spend heavily on thematic research; nothing tested at this price.
why.fmf: Construction economics plus power plus investment analysis - three of her four assets, missing only direct data centre experience.
why.defensibility: Specialist knowledge accumulates, though specialist consultancies already exist here.
why.leverage: One research product serves every subscriber.
why.time_to_revenue: A pilot from her network in 1-3 months.
why.tailwind: AI-driven data centre buildout and the power constraint behind it are the strongest infrastructure themes of the decade.
why.ceiling: £2,000/mo x 9 funds = £216k, and infra funds pay these prices routinely.

ceiling_arithmetic: £2,000/mo x 9 funds = £216k gross on annual contracts, less ~£15k data = £201k net. Only nine clients needed because infra funds pay institutional research prices. Realistic year one: 4-5 = £96-120k.
carries: Only nine customers needed, the strongest infrastructure tailwind available, and a genuine cross-domain angle.
kills: Nothing structural, but she would be entering a specialist field where established consultancies already sell to these funds.
test: Ask two infra fund contacts what they read on data centres and what it costs.
test_pass: They name a gap around construction and power economics.
test_fail: They name a specialist provider they already pay.
